name: Pramlintide
used_for: FDA-labeled (Symlin, NDA 021332, approved 2005) as an add-on treatment for adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin and have not reached glucose goals on optimal insulin. The label carries a boxed warning for severe hypoglycemia when used with insulin. Drugs@FDA currently lists all Symlin products as discontinued, although the label remains on DailyMed. Some online telehealth sites promote it off-label for weight loss, which is not a labeled use.

entries.text: Label: mealtime insulin is reduced by 50% when starting, then Symlin 60 mcg subcutaneously immediately before major meals, increased to 120 mcg before meals if there has been no clinically significant nausea for at least 3 days.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes using mealtime insulin

entries.text: Label: mealtime insulin is reduced by 50% when starting, then Symlin 15 mcg subcutaneously immediately before major meals, increased in 15 mcg steps (to 30, 45 or 60 mcg) if no clinically significant nausea for at least 3 days; reduced if nausea persists.
entries.population: Adults with type 1 diabetes using mealtime insulin

administration_guidance.text: The Symlin label states it is injected subcutaneously immediately before each major meal (at least 250 kcal or 30 g of carbohydrate), into the abdomen or thigh. Arm injection is not recommended because of variable absorption.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Symlin label states the product should be at room temperature before injecting to reduce injection site reactions, sites should be rotated and kept distinct from insulin injection sites, and Symlin is always given as a separate injection and never mixed with insulin.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Symlin label states that if a dose is missed, the next scheduled dose is given at the usual amount, with no make-up dose.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Symlin label states unused pen-injectors are refrigerated (2 to 8 C), protected from light, and not frozen. After first use, a pen may be refrigerated or kept at up to 30 C and is used within 30 days.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: The Symlin label carries a boxed warning of severe hypoglycemia: use with insulin increases the risk, particularly in type 1 diabetes, and when it occurs it is seen within 3 hours after an injection.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Symlin label's pooled trials in type 1 diabetes on insulin, nausea occurred in 48% vs 17% with placebo, anorexia 17% vs 2%, and vomiting 11% vs 7%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the pooled trials in type 2 diabetes on insulin, nausea occurred in 28% vs 12% with placebo, headache 13% vs 7%, anorexia 9% vs 2%, and vomiting 8% vs 4%. The label states nausea is more frequent at the start of treatment.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A peptide information site says pramlintide produced modest weight loss in trials including people without diabetes, but is underused because it needs several daily injections and careful insulin coordination, and newer drugs work better.
A telehealth marketplace page promotes pramlintide for weight loss, citing a 6-week trial with about 2% body weight loss, and advertises appointments within about 24 hours.

research.summary: DailyMed prescribing information for SymlinPen (pramlintide acetate) injection, AstraZeneca (DailyMed version published August 2024).
research.finding: States the approved use as add-on therapy with mealtime insulin, gives the type 1 and type 2 starting doses, and carries a boxed warning that use with insulin raises the risk of severe hypoglycemia.
Shows the original approval on 03/16/2005 and lists all three Symlin products with marketing status Discontinued.

research.summary: 29-week double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 296 adults with type 1 diabetes adding pramlintide to insulin (Edelman et al., Diabetes Care).
research.finding: Average A1C fell by 0.5% in both groups. Pramlintide reduced after-meal glucose spikes and weight (-1.3 kg versus +1.2 kg with placebo). Nausea was more common (63% versus 36%) and severe hypoglycemia was more frequent with pramlintide.

research.summary: Pooled post hoc analysis of two placebo-controlled trials in insulin-using adults with type 2 diabetes whose starting HbA1c was 7.0 to 8.5% (166 people; Hollander et al., Diabetes Obes Metab).
research.finding: At week 26 pramlintide 120 mcg twice daily lowered HbA1c by 0.43% and weight by 2.0 kg more than placebo, without a higher overall rate of severe hypoglycemia. Because this was a post hoc subgroup analysis, it is weaker evidence than the original trials.

research.summary: 16-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in 204 obese adults without insulin treatment, with or without type 2 diabetes, using pramlintide up to 240 mcg three times a day before meals (Aronne et al., Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism).
research.finding: Completers lost 3.7% (3.6 kg) more body weight than placebo, and 88% reached the top dose. Nausea was the most common side effect, and weight loss was similar in people with and without nausea.

research.summary: 6-week randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled trial in 88 obese adults using pramlintide 180 mcg by injection 15 minutes before meals (Smith et al., American Journal of Physiology Endocrinology and Metabolism).
research.finding: Body weight fell 2.1% with pramlintide versus a 0.1% rise with placebo on day 44, and 24-hour calorie intake and portion sizes were lower.

research.summary: 4-month dose-ranging trial in 411 obese adults with a lifestyle program, followed by an 8-month extension for those who chose to continue (Smith et al., Diabetes Care). Six pramlintide regimens (120, 240 or 360 mcg, twice or three times daily) were compared with placebo.
research.finding: Placebo-corrected loss at month 12 was 5.6% (120 mcg three times daily) and 6.8% (360 mcg twice daily). Initial weight loss was regained in the placebo group but mostly kept with pramlintide. Nausea was the most common side effect and was less frequent during the extension.

dose.summary: The Symlin label gives 60 mcg before major meals for type 2 diabetes (up to 120 mcg) and 15 mcg for type 1 diabetes (up to 60 mcg), with mealtime insulin cut by 50% at the start. Weight-loss trials in people without diabetes used 120 to 360 mcg two or three times a day, which is not a labeled use.

fasting.summary: The label limits use to major meals of at least 250 calories or 30 g of carbohydrate. It says to cut mealtime insulin by 50% at the start because of low blood sugar risk.

items.text: The Symlin label states each injection is given only before a major meal of at least 250 kcal or 30 g of carbohydrate. It is not given before smaller meals.
items.label: research

items.text: The Symlin label states that when starting, mealtime insulin doses are reduced by 50% to lower the risk of low blood sugar.
items.label: research

items.text: Klarity, a telehealth seller, says to inject right before each main meal of at least 250 calories or 30 grams of carbohydrate, which matches the label.
items.label: internet

items.text: Doctronic says pramlintide slows digestion and can raise the risk of dangerously low blood sugar, especially with insulin, and advises fast-acting carbohydrate if it happens.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: The label says to inject before each major meal and to skip a missed dose, with no make-up dose. Obesity trials used two or three injections a day. One online site says a missed dose can be taken if the next meal is not close, which differs from the label.

items.text: The Symlin label states that if a dose is missed, the next scheduled dose is given at the usual amount, with no make-up dose.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 4-month obesity trial, three-times-daily and twice-daily regimens both led to weight loss. The 120 mcg three-times-daily and 360 mcg twice-daily regimens kept more weight off at 12 months.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Insight says pramlintide has been considered underused because it needs three daily injections separate from insulin and complex insulin adjustment.
items.label: internet

items.text: Doctronic says a missed dose can be taken if remembered a reasonable time before the next meal, skipped if the next injection is close, and never doubled. The label says to skip it and wait for the next scheduled dose.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Trials ran 16 weeks to 12 months. In the 12-month obesity trial, weight lost early was mostly kept while on pramlintide, and placebo users regained it. Stopping pramlintide was not studied, and no on and off cycling regimen was found.

items.text: In a 29-week placebo-controlled trial in 296 adults with type 1 diabetes, pramlintide reduced weight (-1.3 kg versus +1.2 kg with placebo) and nausea was more common (63% versus 36%).
items.label: research

items.text: In pooled trials in insulin-using adults with type 2 diabetes, at week 26 pramlintide 120 mcg twice daily lowered weight by 2.0 kg more than placebo. This was a post hoc subgroup analysis.
items.label: research

items.text: A 16-week trial in obese adults without insulin found 3.7% placebo-corrected weight loss, and a 6-week trial found 2.1% weight loss on pramlintide.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 12-month obesity trial (8-month extension, 146 evaluable people), early weight loss was regained in the placebo group but maintained with pramlintide in all but the 120 mcg twice daily group.
items.label: research

mechanism.summary: An artificial version of amylin, a hormone made with insulin. It slows stomach emptying, lowers glucagon (a hormone that raises blood sugar) and reduces appetite through the brain.

items.text: The Symlin label describes pramlintide as an amylin analog that slows gastric emptying without changing overall nutrient absorption, suppresses glucagon secretion to reduce liver glucose production, and regulates food intake through centrally mediated appetite effects.
items.label: research

items.text: In an 88-person trial in obese adults, pramlintide lowered 24-hour calorie intake, portion sizes and binge eating scores.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: In obese adults without diabetes, pramlintide gave about 3.7% placebo-corrected weight loss over 16 weeks and 5.6 to 6.8% at 12 months with lifestyle support. Weight loss is not a labeled use, and online sites say newer drugs work better.

items.text: In a 16-week trial in 204 obese adults, pramlintide produced 3.7% (3.6 kg) more weight loss than placebo, and 31% lost at least 5% versus 2% on placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 12-month obesity trial with lifestyle support, placebo-corrected weight loss was 5.6% (120 mcg three times daily) and 6.8% (360 mcg twice daily) at month 12.
items.label: research

items.text: In a 29-week trial in 296 adults with type 1 diabetes, pramlintide reduced after-meal glucose spikes and weight, while average A1C fell 0.5% in both groups.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Insight says pramlintide produced modest weight loss in trials including people without diabetes, and that newer drugs achieve substantially greater results.

side_effect_groups.title: Common
side_effect_groups.summary: Nausea is the most common side effect (48% in type 1 and 28% in type 2 diabetes trials, versus 17% and 12% on placebo), plus loss of appetite, vomiting and headache. It is more frequent at the start.

items.text: In the Symlin label's pooled trials in type 1 diabetes on insulin, nausea occurred in 48% vs 17% with placebo, anorexia 17% vs 2%, and vomiting 11% vs 7%.
items.label: research

items.text: In the pooled trials in type 2 diabetes on insulin, nausea occurred in 28% vs 12% with placebo, headache 13% vs 7%, anorexia 9% vs 2%, and vomiting 8% vs 4%. The label states nausea is more frequent at the start of treatment.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 16-week obesity trial, the most common side effect was mild, transient nausea, and people without nausea lost a similar amount of weight.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Insight says nausea occurs in about 30 to 50% of patients during initiation.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Warnings
side_effect_groups.summary: The label has a boxed warning for severe low blood sugar when used with insulin, which shows up within 3 hours after an injection.

items.text: The Symlin label carries a boxed warning of severe hypoglycemia: use with insulin increases the risk, particularly in type 1 diabetes, and when it occurs it is seen within 3 hours after an injection.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 29-week type 1 diabetes trial, severe hypoglycemia was more frequent with pramlintide than with placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Insight notes the boxed warning for insulin-induced severe hypoglycemia, particularly in type 1 diabetes.
